channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Campanha de Lula evita 'cascas de banana', mas ajustes econômicos devem vir já em 2026
item.description: Lula's re-election campaign aims to avoid negative surprises by announcing fiscal adjustment projects in advance, but signals that structural proposals may only be sent in 2026 if he wins the election. The campaign's economic coordination prioritizes stability and predictability in economic measures, avoiding 'banana peels' that could trigger market volatility.

item.title: O dia seguinte (por André Gustavo Stumpf)
item.description: The 2026 election campaign overlooks Brazil’s severe economic challenges, including debt exceeding R$10 trillion, sub-2% growth, and costly fuel subsidies that strain public finances. Despite looming post-election inflation from subsidy removals, candidates avoid substantive economic proposals, favoring peripheral issues. Victory will go to the least rejected candidate, not the one with the best plan, revealing a culture that prioritizes symbolism over substance.

item.title: Horário eleitoral não é gratuito e custa milhões em renúncia fiscal
item.description: The mandatory electoral broadcast time is not free, as its cost is covered by tax renunciations granted to radio and TV broadcasters in exchange for airing political propaganda. In the 2022 elections, this amounted to R$737 million in tax exemptions, and between 2014 and 2025, the total reached R$5.2 billion. Airtime is distributed unevenly: 10% equally among parties and 90% proportional to the size of each party's caucus in the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Pode investigar. É seu direito. Está na Constituição
item.description: The text critiques the selective application of Brazil's constitutional protection of journalistic source secrecy, arguing that authorities invoke it as a 'shield' to justify rights restrictions when it serves power, but disregard it when it threatens allies or targets opponents. It denounces the hypocrisy of upholding the Constitution only when convenient to the establishment, while silencing journalists, lawmakers, and citizens under pretexts of security or order. The case of journalist Luiz Pablo in Maranhão is framed as another instance of this power logic that erodes rights to protect elites and criminalizes dissent.

item.title: Flávio lidera interações nas redes sobre segurança, e Caiado, número de posts
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) led engagement intentions on public security in digital debates among 2026 presidential candidates, while former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) recorded the highest number of posts on the topic.

item.title: Campanha ganha cara de MMA
item.description: The latest Quaest poll shows Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff has narrowed to just three points, indicating a technical tie. With 50 days until the election, the political climate is heating up, forecasting a period of intense polarization and possible confrontations. The campaign is taking on an aggressive tone, resembling an MMA fight.

item.title: MPSP abre inquérito sobre concessão de rodovias da gestão Tarcísio
item.description: The São Paulo Public Prosecutor's Office has opened a civil inquiry into alleged irregularities in the concession of the Rota Sorocabana and Lote Raposo highways, granted last year, following a complaint by state deputy Reis (PT) regarding lack of public consultation, lack of bidding impartiality, and negative financial and environmental impacts. The São Paulo government denies any illegality, stating that the processes were based on technical studies, transparency, and social participation, including ten public hearings and over 2,800 contributions. The inquiry also notes a possible government withdrawal from installing new tolls on the 'Circuito das Águas' stretch, which sparked protests from local mayors in 2023 over tourism concerns and automated toll systems.

item.title: Flávio entra na mira de campanha, enquanto desgaste de Lula é sabido
item.description: The Quaest poll marks the official start of the 2026 presidential race, with Lula leading in the first round at 38%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 31%. Caiado and Renan Santos each have 4%, and Zema has 2%. In a potential runoff, the race is a technical tie within the margin of error, reflecting deep polarization and the imminent launch of TV advertising and direct confrontations.

item.title: Impostos: diminuir piora
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro promises tax cuts as a presidential candidate, but the policy would be ineffective in Brazil due to the federal structure of taxation, where 80% of revenue comes from states and municipalities. Without spending cuts to offset lost revenue, the measure would worsen the fiscal deficit, undermining confidence, increasing the dollar, inflation, and interest rates. With 96% of federal spending being mandatory, there is little room for adjustment, making the proposal economically disastrous.

item.title: A estratégia de partidos e candidatos para capturar o decisivo ‘voto pragmático’
item.description: The 2026 election will be defined by the contest for the 'pragmatic vote' — voters focused on concrete issues like public safety, health, education, and cost of living, rather than ideological rhetoric. Parties such as the PSB have identified that candidates who prioritize technical solutions and invite non-ideological experts into governance will gain an edge, particularly by emphasizing violence and crime as top priorities. Antisystem candidates — including some governors and former ministers — are gaining traction by criticizing institutions like Congress and the Supreme Court, appealing to evangelicals, female heads of household, and young voters frustrated with bureaucratic inefficiency and state absence.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Lula defended his son against any potential requests to close legal proceedings, stating that no one should seek to dismiss investigations involving him. He encouraged the pursuit of inquiries, saying there is no problem with that, and emphasized that his son should follow his own example of resilience, having spent 580 days in prison and emerged with his head held high.

item.title: A decisão de Moraes contra fonte de jornalista vista nos bastidores do STF
item.description: A decision by Minister Alexandre de Moraes against a former Maranhão secretary, identified as a journalist’s source, raised concerns among STF ministers about violating journalistic source confidentiality, a constitutional ‘petr clause.’ STF President Edson Fachin defended press freedom in plenary, and the case will be reviewed by the First Chamber, with jurists warning of a dangerous precedent.

item.title: Independentes se afastam de Lula, aponta Quaest
item.description: A new Quaest poll shows that independent voters, representing about a third of the Brazilian electorate, have shifted away from Lula (PT) and toward Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in less than ten days. These voters do not firmly identify with either of the two main political poles. The shift highlights increasing volatility among undecided voters in the 2026 election landscape.

item.title: Saiba como funciona o teste de integridade da urna eletrônica
item.description: The electronic voting machine integrity test verifies that the vote recorded by the machine exactly matches the vote cast, by comparing pre-filled paper ballots with the machine’s printed report. Conducted under public supervision by auditors, political parties, and oversight entities, the procedure is standardized by TSE resolutions 23.673/2021 and 23.758/2026 and has been used since 2002 to ensure the accuracy and inviolability of Brazil’s electoral process.

item.title: Roberto Reis na Crusoé: O mito do debate
item.description: The article argues that while television remains a powerful medium in Brazilian elections due to its ability to reach voters in their daily routines, televised debates have limited impact because they require scheduled time and prior interest from the audience. The author warns against equating television with debates, emphasizing that media influence extends far beyond specific candidate confrontations.

item.title: O passado da Vila Euclides, lugar escolhido por Lula e pelo PT para lançar campanha neste domingo
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) held its first official campaign rally of 2026 in Vila Euclides, São Bernardo do Campo, the historic site of Lula's 'Great ABC Strike'. The event marked the launch of the electoral campaign and served as a mobilization test for supporters amid a tightly contested race. Lula, now running for re-election, emphasized his union roots and the PT's legacy in the region.

item.title: Ministro do Trabalho diz que há “falta de recursos humanos” no órgão
item.description: Labor and Employment Minister Luiz Marinho criticized the lack of human and budgetary resources in the Ministry of Labor, stating that the ministry was weakened under Temer and dismantled under Bolsonaro, and is now being reconstructed. He noted progress in restoring labor auditors through dialogue with Minister of Management and Innovation Esther Dweck, emphasizing the need to strengthen the ministry’s administrative backbone despite ongoing challenges.

item.title: E o Banco de Brasília, hein?
item.description: A Metrópoles survey found that 91.2% of 849 readers believe the federal government should not bail out the Bank of Brasília (BRB) from bankruptcy, while only 8.8% support a rescue. The result reflects strong public opposition to using federal funds to aid state-level financial institutions in distress.

item.title: Lulinha e Master são obstáculos para líderes na campanha, que começa amanhã
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign begins tomorrow with President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as the two leading candidates in the polls. Both face distinct challenges in winning over voters in an election expected to be closely contested. Lula must manage evaluations of his government, while Bolsonaro seeks to solidify his position as the main opposition alternative.

item.title: Candidatura de Carlos divide bolsonarismo em SC e expõe limite do sobrenome
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro's Senate candidacy in Santa Catarina is causing divisions within the local Bolsonaro movement, exposing the limits of the family name's influence in the state. Flávio Bolsonaro publicly called for unity, highlighting internal family and political tensions over electoral strategy.

item.title: Mortes de crianças caem, mas violência policial avança, diz Unicef
item.description: Child and adolescent deaths due to police action rose 3.9% in 2025, accounting for 23.1% of all deaths in this age group, despite an overall 10.8% decline in intentional violent deaths. Unicef and the Brazilian Forum on Public Security launched a manifesto for the 2026 elections, urging candidates to prioritize protective parenting, combat extreme violence and racism, and ensure sustainable budget allocation for child protection policies.

item.title: Governador do MA diz sofrer perseguição de Flávio Dino no STF
item.description: Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão accused Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino of political persecution after Dino authorized a Federal Police investigation targeting Brandão’s allies, including Senator Weverton Rocha and TCE-MA president Daniel Brandão, his nephew. Brandão argues the case should be handled by the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), not the STF, and claims Dino is biased for having endorsed Felipe Camarão, his political rival, in the 2026 gubernatorial race. The two, once allies who won together in 2018 and 2022, split in 2024, dividing the state’s government into opposing factions.

item.title: Antes da TV, Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro abrem campanha com estratégias opostas nas redes e nas ruas
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign kicks off with Lula emphasizing his government's legacy and national sovereignty, contrasting his administration with Jair Bolsonaro's. Flávio Bolsonaro aims to undermine Lula by highlighting corruption allegations and expanding his appeal beyond the bolsonarist base without radicalizing his rhetoric. The race will also be the first test of the TSE's new rules on artificial intelligence use in electoral campaigns.

item.title: Flávio lidera interações nas redes sobre segurança, e Caiado, número de publicações, diz estudo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro led social media interactions on public security with over one million engagements, while Ronaldo Caiado published the most on the topic (32 posts). The PL party dominated the digital debate with 46% of total engagement, compared to the PT's 8.1%, although Lula's allies were prominent in femicide discussions.

item.title: Flávio planeja agenda no Rio no mesmo dia que Lula
item.description: President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are scheduling campaign events in Rio de Janeiro on the same day, August 22, a Saturday. Lula will hold a rally at the Bangu stadium in the West Zone, while Flávio will host an event at the Gilberto Cardoso gymnasium, known as Maracanãzinho, in the city center. The day before, Flávio plans a walk through the Baixada Fluminense followed by a dinner with mayors, and Lula will have an agenda in Belo Horizonte on Friday, August 21, to support the launch of Patrus Ananias’s candidacy for Minas Gerais governor.

item.title: Flávio recorre a símbolos de Bolsonaro na largada da campanha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) launches his presidential campaign with an act at Copacabana Beach, replicating the symbols and mobilization strategies of former President Jair Bolsonaro, including green and yellow clothing and appeals to bolsonarismo. The event marks the first day of authorized electoral propaganda and reinforces Flávio’s effort to revive his father’s campaign style, which previously used the beachfront for large political rallies, including attacks on the STF and calls for military intervention. The strategy aims to mobilize the bolsonarist base through symbolic echoes of key moments from the 2022 campaign.

item.title: Kassab aposta reputação contra Flávio e vê Centrão fechado com Lula
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, stated that Flávio Bolsonaro has 'zero' chance of being elected president and will 'collapse' once the PT and official campaign expose his weaknesses. Kassab added that Centrão parties are already aligned with Lula, ruling out any real neutrality, as they prefer the predictability of negotiations with the Planalto over backing a candidacy seen as fragile and lacking political stamina.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1: pressão do PT sobre o Senado ‘atrapalhou’, diz líder do governo na Casa sobre acelerar votação
item.description: The government leader in the Senate, Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), acknowledged that the PT's pressure on Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) to speed up the vote on ending the 6x1 scale backfired and disrupted the process. However, she said there is an 'implicit commitment' from the senator to advance the issue following his meeting with President Lula.

item.title: Prazo para registro de candidaturas termina neste sábado (15/8)
item.description: Political parties, federations, and coalitions must register their candidacies for the 2026 general elections by 7 p.m. this Saturday (August 15), covering positions such as president, governor, senator, and federal and state deputies. The deadline ends the pre-campaign period, allowing official campaigning to begin on Sunday (August 16), with the first round set for October 4. Additionally, the deadline applies to opening specific bank accounts for donations and submitting criteria for the use of funds to the TSE.

item.title: SP com 110 vagas, RR com 1: a Câmara se todos os votos valessem igual
item.description: The Brazilian Constitution sets minimum (8) and maximum (70) seats per state in the Chamber of Deputies, distorting vote equality. As a result, a vote in Roraima today carries eight times the weight of a vote in São Paulo. If votes were weighted equally, São Paulo would have 110 deputies (instead of 70), Roraima would have just one, and other states would gain or lose seats, sparking debate over reforming the system to better balance population-based representation with federal principles.

item.title: Julgamento de ação do PT no TSE trava repasses do fundo eleitoral a partidos, que traçam estratégias para a verba
item.description: A TSE halted the distribution of R$ 4.9 billion in electoral funds after the PT filed a motion to recount its congressional delegation to include 69 deputies elected in 2022 instead of the current 68. While rapporteur Nunes Marques opposed the request, Minister Estela Aranha requested a view, stalling the analysis and blocking the release of 48% of the fund pending a final ruling.

item.title: Nova pesquisa Quaest reduz vantagem de Lula sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no Rali; veja os números
item.description: The Quaest poll, integrated into the Rali aggregator (GLOBO/Instituto Locomotiva), showed a reduction in President Lula's lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 presidential race. Specific numbers from the poll were not disclosed in the provided excerpt, but the trend indicates a tightening competition between the two candidates. The content is exclusive to GLOBO subscribers.

item.title: De gênero a idade e religião: os grupos que rejeitam mais ou menos Lula e Flávio na pesquisa Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula faces highest rejection in the Southeast (62%) and South (57%), while Flávio Bolsonaro is most rejected in the Northeast (63%). Lula's rejection is higher among women (50%), ages 16–34 (56%), those with higher education (61%), and income above five minimum wages (61%). Flávio Bolsonaro's rejection peaks among low-income earners (62%), those with up to elementary education (61%), and those aged 60 or older (57%).

item.title: Voto a voto: Quaest reforça corrida acirrada, e Lula e Flávio iniciam a campanha empatados na margem de erro no 2º turno
item.description: The Quaest poll, commissioned by TV Globo and GLOBO, shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the projected 2026 runoff, with Lula at 43% and Bolsonaro at 40%. The data reflect a highly competitive race, to be decided vote by vote, at the campaign’s outset. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Planos de governo dos presidenciáveis ampliam promessas na área econômica, mas não detalham impacto nas contas públicas
item.description: Presidential candidates' government plans expanded promises of economic growth, investment, and improved public finances, but failed to provide consolidated estimates of the fiscal impact of their proposals. Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) plan emphasizes a 'tesouraço' with spending cuts and tax reductions, yet simultaneously proposes new spending in health, security, infrastructure, and social care without detailing how these costs will be offset. The lack of a unified fiscal account leaves the path to fulfilling these promises unclear.

item.title: Quaest: Lula vê piora de desempenho entre eleitores independentes, apontados como decisivos na escolha do presidente
item.description: The Quaest poll shows that independent voters, who make up a third of the electorate and are pivotal in the 2026 presidential race, are drifting away from Lula and moving toward Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro’s support among independents rose from 30% to 35%, while Lula’s fell from 33% to 29%, with all shifts favoring the opposition candidate. Furthermore, 36% of independents now view Lula’s government negatively, surpassing those who see it as regular (34%), and 58% believe Brazil is heading in the wrong direction.

item.title: Weverton nega tentativa de interferência em investigações da PF
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) denied attempting to interfere in Federal Police investigations, stating his communications with ministers are institutional and that the case against him stems from an irresponsible complaint. He is targeted by Operation Sem Desconto, which investigates INSS fraud, and also probed for alleged intervention in an STJ case linked to the MA Court of Accounts. Justice Flávio Dino lifted secrecy on rulings authorizing the investigation, after Weverton recorded with President Lula for the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Descaso fiscal é a alma da nova lei dos combustíveis
item.description: The Lula government and Congress approved the Fuel PLP, using Treasury resources to subsidize gasoline and diesel amid rising oil prices due to the Middle East war, revealing disregard for public finances. The measure includes an export tax on petroleum to offset diesel costs but relies on federal funds to keep gasoline cheap at the pump.

item.title: Queda da fila do INSS acelera nos últimos meses; benefícios negados sobem e chegam a quase 1 milhão em junho
item.description: The INSS benefit waiting list dropped to 1.55 million in July, the lowest level in 21 months, with a 74% reduction year-to-date. However, benefit denials surged, nearing 1 million in June and rising 70% compared to the same period last year, particularly for disability-related benefits. Experts warn this approach may merely shift demand to judicialization, as many denied claims could lead to new applications, administrative appeals, or court actions.

item.title: Assassinatos de indígenas aumentam durante governo Lula
item.description: Indigenous killings in Brazil rose in 2025 for the third consecutive year, according to a report by the Indigenist Missionary Council (Cimi), linked to the Catholic Church. The increase occurred during the government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, despite his promises to protect Indigenous peoples.

item.title: Petrobras encontra sinais de petróleo na bacia da Foz do Amazonas - por que projeto de exploração ali é controverso?
item.description: Petrobras has found indications of oil in the Foz do Amazonas basin, in ultra-deep waters off Amapá, though economic viability remains unconfirmed. The project is controversial due to the region's ecological sensitivity and opposition from environmental groups, despite support from the Lula government and Petrobras's claims of technological safety and energy demand fulfillment.

item.title: Governador do MA diz estar sendo julgado por um adversário político
item.description: Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão (MDB) challenged Minister Flávio Dino's STF decision lifting secrecy on PF investigations into corruption, embezzlement, witness intimidation, and obstruction of justice involving state political leaders, arguing the STF lacks jurisdiction over governors and that he is being politically targeted by an adversary ahead of the 2026 elections. He also criticized the investigation's temporal focus, claiming it omits the 2019 reopening of a 2014 administrative payment process for R$ 800 million owed to SH Vigilância — allegedly the true motive behind the 2022 killing of João Bosco Sobrinho Pereira de Oliveira.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede a Moraes para ir a dentista e indica mulher de Flávio
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's defense requested authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for the former president to attend a dental appointment on August 21 at 2:00 p.m. at the Terracota Clinical Center in Brasília. The dentist named is Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The request comes despite a 30-day visitation ban, with exceptions for health professionals, and follows Moraes’ restriction on political visits after Bolsonaro published a letter endorsing Flávio as his 'spokesperson' in the presidential race.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede ao STF autorização para ir a consulta odontológica com mulher de Flávio
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro has requested authorization from the STF to temporarily leave house arrest for a dental appointment next Friday. The dentist indicated by his defense is Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, wife of his son Flávio Bolsonaro, who is currently barred from visiting him under a 90-day restriction ordered by Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The defense argues the leave would be strictly for the appointment, subject to relevant monitoring measures.

item.title: TSE remarca reunião sobre IA de Bolsonaro para 3ª feira
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has rescheduled a private meeting for Tuesday, August 18, 2026, to discuss whether an AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro constitutes a prohibited deepfake under Resolution 23.732/2024. Minister Nunes Marques aims to establish a precedent on AI use in electoral campaigns, as the PT claims the video, used during Flávio Bolsonaro’s convention, violates electoral rules despite being positive in tone. The case is also under review by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) following allegations of judicial non-compliance by Bolsonaro.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede ao STF para ir à dentista e indica esposa de Flávio para atendimento
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro requested STF authorization to leave house arrest for a dental appointment, naming his daughter-in-law Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro — wife of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro — as his treating dentist. The appointment is scheduled for March 21 at 2:00 p.m. Bolsonaro is serving house arrest following a conviction for a coup plot and is recovering from bacterial pneumonia.

item.title: Flávio é o candidato mais rejeitado, aponta Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is the most rejected presidential candidate according to a Quaest poll released on March 14, with 54% of respondents rejecting him. He is followed by President Lula (PT) at 52% rejection and former governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at 35%. The poll also lists former governor Romeu Zema as the next in line.

item.title: ‘Eles articularam’: Marina Silva responsabiliza família Bolsonaro pelo tarifaço
item.description: Marina Silva, the Rede Sustentabilidade candidate for the Senate from São Paulo, stated that the U.S. tariff hike harms strategic sectors of São Paulo's economy, including footwear, auto parts, coffee, and biofuels, and attributed it to the Bolsonaro family's articulation, which, she said, fails to separate political interests from national strategic interests. She also criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for not joining the Propag program, which she said caused a loss of nearly R$ 11 billion, and argued that Brazil cannot accept economic losses driven by political interests.

item.title: Kassab reafirma que Flávio não vence eleição e diz que centrão favorece PT
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD and running mate of Ronaldo Caiado, reaffirmed that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will not win the 2026 presidential election and stated that centrist leaders support Lula's (PT) reelection. His remarks highlight internal fractures on the right and suggest a broad coalition forming around the current government.

item.title: Novas imagens mostram aproximação da PM a motorista de Haddad
item.description: New images released by São Paulo's SSP show a police cruiser slowly passing by the car of Fernando Haddad's driver on Joinville Street, but they do not confirm any interaction or approach. The SSP reiterated there is no evidence of irregular procedure, after analyzing over 40 security cameras and vehicle geolocation data. The incident has intensified campaign tensions, with Haddad suggesting political persecution by his rival, Tarcísio de Freitas.
